bugs.title: Deploy-failure Telegram alert silently skips itself on clones because BOTB_MTPROTO_BOT_TOKEN secret is unset
bugs.notes: Seeded 2026-08-28. Confirmed via a real failed Deploy Bots run on clone motionssalt/clipforge-clone-y59fyk: the alert step (bug-58) detects missing BOTB_MTPROTO_BOT_TOKEN, logs a warning to the Actions log, and exits 0 without notifying anyone. Clone owners get no Telegram notification of blocked deploys. Fix must ensure a clone owner whose Deploy Bots run fails actually receives a Telegram alert; investigate how clone secrets/bot tokens are provisioned before choosing approach. [in_progress 2026-08-28] Beginning investigation: reading deploy workflow alert step, clone provisioning flow, and bot token secret patterns. [done 2026-08-28] ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED by code read: the bug-58 alert step in .github/workflows/deploy-bots.yml posts from the Actions runner using secrets.BOTB_MTPROTO_BOT_TOKEN, which exists ONLY on the central repo — ARCHITECTURE.md §9.2 marks the BOTB_MTPROTO_*/relay subsystem central-only, and §10 states one shared Bot A deployment serves all users, so clones have NO bot token of their own and nothing in clone creation (createPrivateShadowClone) provisions Actions secrets other than GEMINI_API_KEYS during onboarding. Therefore the fix could NOT be another clone repo secret: (a) no provisioning touchpoint exists for a Telegram token, and (b) writing the central Bot B token into a clone secret would hand a central credential to a repo whose workflow files the clone owner controls (§13 violation). CHOSEN FIX — two parts. (1) bot/src: the shared Bot A now polls the CONNECTED repo's deploy-bots.yml runs with the owner's own PAT via new listWorkflowRuns() (github.js), on the home-screen touchpoint in showHome (commands/start.js#announceDeployFailure) — the same passive-pull pattern as bug-46 news and bug-65 auto-update, chosen because the worker has no cron trigger and the central account cannot push into a private clone. Each failed run is DMed to the clone owner exactly once; the KV marker (getAnnouncedDeployFailure/setAnnouncedDeployFailure in storage.js) is the run id (not sha) so a rerun that fails again still notifies, and it is stored only after a successful send so transient failures retry on the next home render. Best-effort, try/catch — never blocks the home screen; main-account chats are excluded (isOriginalRepo) since the central repo already has the real-time workflow alert. The message includes the failing run URL and notes that failure is expected on a brand-new clone before Cloudflare credentials are configured. (2) workflow: when BOTB_MTPROTO_BOT_TOKEN is absent (a clone), the alert step now exits 1 after logging the pointer instead of silently exiting 0, so a failed clone run stays visibly red in the Actions UI rather than showing a green 'alert' step; on the central repo the step is unchanged and still sends the real-time Telegram alert. VERIFICATION: node --check passes on github.js/storage.js/start.js; bot test suite 110 pass / 0 fail (the 5 pre-existing failures recorded in bug-65's notes no longer reproduce — they were fixed in an earlier landed change; regardless, no new failures from this change). End-to-end delivery on a live clone requires the deployed Bot A Worker to pick this up (deploy-bots.yml triggers on bot/** push) and the clone owner to open the bot home screen after a failed run — that is the designed delivery path, consistent with bug-46/bug-65.
